newsitem.title: JAPAN: Deregulation to boost Japan GDP growth 0.9 pct - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Deregulation to boost Japan GDP growth 0.9 pct - EPA.

text.p: Deregulation would boost growth in Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) by an average of about 0.9 percent per year in the years from 1998/99 to 2003/04, the Economic Planning Agency said on Thursday.

The EPA said in a statement that the agency calculated the possible positive effect on the economy of Japan's programme of deregulation and economic reforms, including so-called "Big Bang" financial reforms.

If the reforms are carried out, the ratio of Japan's current account surplus to GDP would be cut by 0.9 percent by 2003/04 due to an expected expansion in domestic demand and a resulting increase in imports, the statement said.
Deregulation would also help lower Japan's production costs, bringing down consumer prices by an average rate of about 1.2 percent per year from 1998/99 to 2003/04.
Japan's unemployment rate would rise by about 0.3 percent by 2003/04 without deregulation in the labour market, EPA said.

It added that deregulation would increase private housing investment by an average of 1.3 percent annually during the six-year period, while it would boost private capital investment by 1.2 percent per year.
